conflicts: Pm ground-level A(147Pm): measured 620.3(14) MHz (452 nm line) / 619.4(17) MHz (468 nm line), weighted mean 619.9(7) MHz (Studer et al. 2020); the older value 647(13) MHz used by Reader et al. was an estimate scaled from the 6H7/2 atomic-beam data, not a measurement.
Pm ground-level A from the two lines disagrees for the light isotopes: 143Pm 1368.9(25) vs 1363.9(29) MHz; 144Pm 329.0(12) vs 322.0(56) MHz (the authors call the significance low).
Pm level energies: the paper prints 22080.06 and 21348.21 cm^-1, NIST lists 22080.08 and 21348.22 cm^-1.

147Pm magnetic moment: 2.58(7) nuclear magnetons (Reader / IAEA table) versus 2.57(4) re-evaluated weighted mean and 2.51(5) from the Goudsmit-Fermi-Segre re-evaluation in Studer et al. 2020; the 1963 atomic-beam abstract gives |mu| = 3.2(3).
not_found: radiative lifetimes of the Pm I levels the site draws (20006.04 - 28274.21 cm^-1): no measurement located; only the 22080.08 level has a (rough) value. For 21348.22 the paper only says the lifetime is much shorter than the laser pulse (40-60 ns), no number
transition probabilities / branching ratios / oscillator strengths of Pm I lines: none located (NIST has none either)
absolute transition frequencies of the 452 nm and 468 nm lines: not printed in the paper (only isotope shifts relative to 147Pm)
hyperfine constants of any other Pm I level; hyperfine constants of the ground level 6H5/2 before 2020 were estimates
Studer et al., Phys. Rev. A 99, 062513 (2019) (level list, ionisation potential): the open-access PDF could not be downloaded by script; not used
laser cooling: none exists for Pm (all isotopes radioactive); the 'use' annotations refer to resonance-ionisation spectroscopy
notes: All hyperfine constants and isotope shifts are from one experiment (in-source resonance-ionisation spectroscopy, PI-LIST, Mainz), linewidth 100-250 MHz. Errors include the authors' extra 1 MHz (A) and 10 MHz (B). B of the 21348.22 and 22080.08 levels for 143-146Pm are dependent fit parameters. Isotope-shift keys follow the schema: nu(first) - nu(second), i.e. nu(147) - nu(A'). Upper-level J values (5/2 for 22080.08, 7/2 for 21348.22) were read from the paper's Fig. 3 and agree with NIST. Level energies of the ionisation schemes were read from an equation image in the article. Neither the 452 nm nor the 468 nm line is among the transitions the site currently draws (those are the strongest NIST lines 473-515 nm), for which no measured data beyond NIST exist.
